Rather than attempting to establish the underlying mechanism, this paper presents two empirical scaling relations that predict dissipation heat (F) and average wind speed (v) from a planet's rotation, gravity, and axial tilt, and validates them—normalized to Jupiter, with zero free parameters—across six planets (Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune). Gas giants and ice giants agree with the predicted values within the stated error margins, whereas rocky planets show deviations; part of this deviation is accounted for by a known additional contribution. The fact that these relations hold with zero free parameters suggests that they may carry physical significance, although their exact origin lies beyond the scope of this paper.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.22541/essoar.15006447/v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 7, 22]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "3e6ad50c235c64f64917304f9a9fe62462dbb4117c5b5d5…
